```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

movies <- read_csv("data/movies.csv")
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
movies_clean <- movies |>
  separate_rows(genre, sep = ", ")
```

```{r}
ggplot(movies, aes(x = tomatoMeter)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Tomatometer Scores",
    subtitle = paste("Number of films:", nrow(movies)),
    x = "Tomatometer Score",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

```{r}
movies_gap <- movies_clean |>
  filter(tomatoMeter != 0, audienceScore != 0) |>
  mutate(gap = tomatoMeter - audienceScore)

movies_summary <- movies_gap |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarize(
    mean_gap = mean(gap, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 100) |>
  arrange(mean_gap)

movies_summary
```

```{r}
ggplot(movies_summary, aes(x = mean_gap, y = reorder(genre, -mean_gap))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Audience and Critics Often Disagree by Genre",
    subtitle = "Mean Tomatometer-minus-audience score gap; negative values favor audiences.",
    x = "Mean score gap",
    y = NULL
  )
```

```{r}
spiderman <- movies |>
  filter(title %in% c(
    "Spider-Man", "Spider-Man 2", "Spider-Man 3",
    "The Amazing Spider-Man", "The Amazing Spider-Man 2",
    "Spider-Man: Homecoming", "Spider-Man: Far From Home",
    "Spider-Man: No Way Home"
  )) |>
  arrange(releaseDateTheaters) |>
  mutate(title = factor(title, levels = title))

spiderman |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(tomatoMeter, audienceScore),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  mutate(score_type = recode(
    score_type,
    tomatoMeter = "Critics",
    audienceScore = "Audiences"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = title, y = score, color = score_type, group = score_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Audience scores exceeded critic scores for four of the eight Spider-Man films",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Score",
    color = "Score"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
